source: Morais O., Cargill C., Parke K. and Barnes T. 2020. Smallholder Pig Production Technicians' Manual. Timor-Leste Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, University of Queensland, ACIAR and the TOMAK Program (Australian Aid), Dili.
text: Sow feeding amounts should change through the reproductive cycle. During pregnancy: 2.5 kg/day from mating to 5 weeks gestation, rising to 3.0 kg/day (5–8 weeks), 3.6 kg/day (8–13 weeks), and 4.0 kg/day (13 weeks to 5 days before farrowing) — each split into two feeds. In the final run-up to farrowing, cut back to 2.6 kg/day (5 days to 1 day pre-farrowing) then 1.0 kg/day on the day before farrowing. After farrowing: no food on day 1, then 0.8 kg on day 2, increasing by 0.8 kg/day up to 5.6 kg/day by day 8, then feeding at least twice daily averaging 5–7 kg/day (depending on sow size and litter size) from day 9 until weaning. After weaning, feed at least 3kg/day (more for larger sows) until she's mated again.
caveat: This guidance comes from a Timor-Leste smallholder pig manual, not a Cambodia-specific source. Feed ingredients and general husbandry practices transfer well to Cambodia's tropical smallholder conditions, but local breed weights/ages and disease-context details may differ; confirm specifics with a local vet or extension officer where precision matters.
